# Compatibility fixtures

Each `vX.Y.Z/` directory holds a data directory written by that cachydb
release and the logical content it must read as:

- `data/` — the data directory, written by the release's own engine:
  two databases (`kb`, `shop`); collections with and without a schema;
  a scalar index (`by_prio`, `by_cat`) and an array-field index
  (`by_tags`); documents with nested objects and arrays; updates and
  deletes; tiny data segments, so at least one segment is sealed (with a
  hint file); and an unflushed tail that is only in the write-ahead log
  (the generator exits without `Close`, as a crash would).
- `expected.jsonl` — the expected content in the export format
  (`cachydb utils export`), computed by the generator from the
  operations it performed, not by exporting with any engine.

`TestCompatFixtures` (`pkg/db/compat_test.go`) copies each `data/` to a
temporary directory, opens it with the current engine, and checks that
the export equals `expected.jsonl` (the header's `created` and
`cachydb` fields are ignored), that every index answers `eq`, `has` and
counts like a scan, and that the upgraded directory takes writes and
reopens. v0.0.4 wrote index snapshots in format v1, so it also covers the
rebuild to v2.

Never edit a fixture by hand, and never regenerate an existing one: it
is the bytes that release wrote.

## Adding the fixture of a release

Every release adds its fixture, generated by the release's own code with
`test/compat/gen` (which uses only the engine API that exists since
v0.0.4). From the repository root, after tagging `vX.Y.Z`:

```bash
v=vX.Y.Z
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
git worktree add --detach "$tmp/wt" "$v"
mkdir -p "$tmp/wt/test/compat/gen"
cp test/compat/gen/main.go "$tmp/wt/test/compat/gen/main.go"   # the current generator
(cd "$tmp/wt" && go run ./test/compat/gen -out "$tmp/$v" -version "$v")
cp -r "$tmp/$v" "pkg/db/testdata/compat/$v"
git worktree remove --force "$tmp/wt"
rm -rf "$tmp"
go test -run TestCompatFixtures ./pkg/db/
```

Keep each fixture small (about 200 KB at most; the current ones are
about 124 KB). If a future engine API drops something the generator
uses, keep the old calls working in the generator for older tags, or
note the adaptation here.

The v0.0.4 and v0.0.5 fixtures were generated this way from the tags
`v0.0.4` (`656005a`) and `v0.0.5` (`daca77c`). Both releases have every
option the generator uses (including `DataSegmentSize` and
`FlushInterval`), so no adaptation was needed.
